418	def _breaking_changes_with_impact(
419	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
420	    base_row: sqlite3.Row,
421	    target_row: sqlite3.Row,
422	) -> list[dict]:
423	    """Breaking-change entries of the target version against the base.
424	
425	    Shared by the pairwise compatibility impact check and the per-dataset
426	    evolution summary. A breaking change is exactly one of ``removed``,
427	    ``type_changed`` or ``nullable_tightened``; a field with several changes
428	    collapses into one entry, a type change winning over a nullable
429	    tightening. Each entry additionally carries ``impacted``: every field
430	    directly or indirectly downstream of the broken field along the lineage
431	    mappings. The traversal starts from the same-named field of the base
432	    version and, when the field still exists in the target version, also from
433	    the target version's field; the merged set is deduplicated, never
434	    contains a start field itself (cycles terminate) and is sorted by
435	    dataset, version and field ascending. Entries are sorted by field name.
436	    """
437	    base_fields = _version_field_definitions(conn, base_row["id"])
438	    target_fields = _version_field_definitions(conn, target_row["id"])
439	
440	    breaking_changes: list[dict] = []
441	    for name in sorted(set(base_fields) | set(target_fields)):
442	        before = base_fields.get(name)
443	        after = target_fields.get(name)
444	        if before is None:
445	            # Added in the target: never breaking.
446	            continue
447	        if after is None:
448	            kind = "removed"
449	        elif before["type"] != after["type"]:
450	            kind = "type_changed"
451	        elif before["nullable"] and not after["nullable"]:
452	            kind = "nullable_tightened"
453	        else:
454	            continue
455	
456	        # The base version always has the broken field; the target version's
457	        # same-named field joins the traversal only when it still exists.
458	        start_ids = [_field_id_by_name(conn, base_row["id"], name)]
459	        if after is not None:
460	            start_ids.append(_field_id_by_name(conn, target_row["id"], name))
461	        impacted = _compute_impacted_multi(
462	            conn, [field_id for field_id in start_ids if field_id is not None]
463	        )
464	
465	        breaking_changes.append(
466	            {
467	                "field": name,
468	                "kind": kind,
469	                "before": before,
470	                "after": after,
471	                "impacted": impacted,
472	            }
473	        )
474	    return breaking_changes

477	def check_schema_version_compatibility_impact(
478	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
479	    dataset_name: str,
480	    base_version: int,
481	    target_version: int,
482	    *,
483	    body: bytes = b"",
484	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
485	) -> dict:
486	    """Read-only breaking-change check joined with downstream lineage impact.
487	
488	    The breaking changes are exactly those of
489	    :func:`check_schema_version_compatibility` (``removed``, ``type_changed``
490	    or ``nullable_tightened``; a field with several changes collapses into one
491	    entry, a type change winning over a nullable tightening), and each entry
492	    additionally carries ``impacted``: every field directly or indirectly
493	    downstream of the broken field along the lineage mappings. The traversal
494	    starts from the same-named field of the base version and, when the field
495	    still exists in the target version, also from the target version's field;
496	    the merged set is deduplicated, never contains a start field itself
497	    (cycles terminate) and is sorted by dataset, version and field ascending.
498	    A field with no downstream yields an empty list; comparing a version with
499	    itself yields an empty entry list and a zero count.
500	
501	    The endpoint takes no parameters: a non-positive version number is a 422
502	    checked before path resolution, while any request body bytes (including
503	    whitespace-only bytes) or any query parameter is a 422 raised only after
504	    the path dataset and both versions have resolved, so an unknown
505	    dataset/version stays a 404 (mirroring the compatibility endpoint).
506	    Nothing is written: version definitions, lineage mappings and the impact
507	    cache are all left untouched.
508	    """
509	    if base_version < 1 or target_version < 1:
510	        raise RequestInvalidError(
511	            "Version numbers in the compatibility path must be positive integers"
512	        )
513	
514	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
515	    base_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, base_version)
516	    target_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, target_version)
517	
518	    if body:
519	        raise RequestInvalidError(
520	            "The version compatibility impact endpoint does not accept a "
521	            "request body"
522	        )
523	    if query_keys:
524	        raise RequestInvalidError(
525	            "The version compatibility impact endpoint does not accept query "
526	            "parameters"
527	        )
528	
529	    breaking_changes = _breaking_changes_with_impact(conn, base_row, target_row)
530	    return {
531	        "base_version": base_row["version"],
532	        "target_version": target_row["version"],
533	        "breaking_changes": breaking_changes,
534	        "breaking_change_count": len(breaking_changes),
535	    }

542	
543	def summarize_schema_version_evolution(
544	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
545	    dataset_name: str,
546	    *,
547	    body: bytes = b"",
548	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
549	) -> dict:
550	    """Read-only summary of adjacent-version breaking changes and impact.
551	
552	    One entry per adjacent version pair of the dataset, ordered by base
553	    version number ascending; a pair with no breaking change is listed with
554	    zero counts. The breaking entries of a pair are exactly those of
555	    :func:`check_schema_version_compatibility_impact` (``removed``,
556	    ``type_changed`` or ``nullable_tightened``, several changes of one field
557	    collapsing into a single entry) and ``breaking_count`` is their number.
558	    The pair's impacted set is the union of every entry's downstream fields —
559	    same start-field rule as the pairwise impact response, merged and
560	    deduplicated, never containing a start field itself (cycles terminate) —
561	    and ``impacted_count`` is its size; ``impacted_datasets`` lists the
562	    distinct dataset names appearing in it, sorted ascending. ``totals``
563	    counts the pairs and sums the per-pair breaking and deduplicated impacted
564	    counts over the whole dataset. A dataset with fewer than two versions
565	    yields an empty pair list and all-zero totals, never an error.
566	
567	    The summary is recomputed from the persisted definitions and lineage
568	    mappings on every read: it caches nothing and never writes, so version
569	    definitions, lineage mappings and the impact cache are all left
570	    untouched, and quality or privacy state plays no role. The dataset
571	    resolves first (404); any request body bytes (including whitespace-only
572	    bytes) or any query parameter is a 422 checked afterwards, and every
573	    ordering is computed explicitly rather than read from database order.
574	    """
575	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
576	
577	    if body:
578	        raise RequestInvalidError(
579	            "The schema evolution summary endpoint does not accept a "
580	            "request body"
581	        )
582	    if query_keys:
583	        raise RequestInvalidError(
584	            "The schema evolution summary endpoint does not accept query "
585	            "parameters"
586	        )
587	
588	    version_rows = conn.execute(
589	        "SELECT id, version FROM schema_versions WHERE dataset_id = ?",
590	        (dataset["id"],),
591	    ).fetchall()
592	    ordered = sorted(version_rows, key=lambda row: row["version"])
593	
594	    pairs: list[dict] = []
595	    for base_row, target_row in zip(ordered, ordered[1:]):
596	        breaking_changes = _breaking_changes_with_impact(conn, base_row, target_row)
597	        impacted_refs = {
598	            (item["dataset"], item["version"], item["field"])
599	            for change in breaking_changes
600	            for item in change["impacted"]
601	        }
602	        pairs.append(
603	            {
604	                "base_version": base_row["version"],
605	                "target_version": target_row["version"],
606	                "breaking_count": len(breaking_changes),
607	                "impacted_count": len(impacted_refs),
608	                "impacted_datasets": sorted({ref[0] for ref in impacted_refs}),
609	            }
610	        )
611	
612	    totals = {
613	        "pair_count": len(pairs),
614	        "breaking_count": sum(pair["breaking_count"] for pair in pairs),
615	        "impacted_count": sum(pair["impacted_count"] for pair in pairs),
616	    }
617	    return {"dataset": dataset["name"], "pairs": pairs, "totals": totals}

624	
625	def _field_status_change(before: dict | None, after: dict | None) -> str:
626	    """Status literal of one field between two adjacent versions.
627	
628	    The literals reuse the breaking-entry vocabulary of the compatibility
629	    check (``removed``, ``type_changed``, ``nullable_tightened``) extended
630	    with the non-breaking outcomes: ``added`` when the field appears on the
631	    target side, ``nullable_loosened`` when only the nullability relaxes and
632	    ``unchanged`` when both definitions agree (including both absent).
633	    Several changes of one field collapse into a single status, a type
634	    change winning over a nullable tightening (mirrors the breaking-entry
635	    rule of the compatibility check).
636	    """
637	    if before is None:
638	        return "added" if after is not None else "unchanged"
639	    if after is None:
640	        return "removed"
641	    if before == after:
642	        return "unchanged"
643	    if before["type"] != after["type"]:
644	        return "type_changed"
645	    if before["nullable"] and not after["nullable"]:
646	        return "nullable_tightened"
647	    return "nullable_loosened"
648	
649	
650	def get_field_trajectory(
651	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
652	    dataset_name: str,
653	    field_name: str,
654	    *,
655	    body: bytes = b"",
656	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
657	) -> dict:
658	    """Read-only cross-version trajectory of one field of a dataset.
659	
660	    ``entries`` lists every schema version of the dataset ordered by version
661	    number ascending, each carrying the field's persisted definition in that
662	    version (only ``type`` and ``nullable``) or ``None`` — key retained —
663	    when the field does not exist there. ``changes`` lists one entry per
664	    adjacent version pair, ordered by base version ascending; each entry
665	    carries the pair's ``status`` (see :func:`_field_status_change`) and the
666	    field's downstream impact for that pair, computed with the same
667	    start-field rule as the compatibility impact response: the traversal
668	    starts from the base version's same-named field and, when the field
669	    exists in the target version, also from the target version's field. The
670	    impacted set is deduplicated, never contains a start field itself
671	    (cycles terminate), is sorted by dataset, version and field ascending
672	    and is empty when the field has no downstream; ``impacted_datasets``
673	    lists the distinct dataset names appearing in it, sorted ascending. A
674	    dataset with fewer than two versions yields an empty change list, never
675	    an error.
676	
677	    Only the persisted version field definitions and lineage mappings are
678	    read; quality, privacy, snapshot and processing-task state play no
679	    role. The trajectory is recomputed on every read: it caches nothing and
680	    never writes, so version definitions, lineage mappings and the impact
681	    cache are all left untouched, and every ordering is computed explicitly
682	    rather than read from database order.
683	
684	    The dataset resolves first (404), then the field must appear in at
685	    least one of the dataset's versions (404); any request body bytes
686	    (including whitespace-only bytes) or any query parameter is a 422
687	    checked afterwards, so both 404 cases keep precedence over the request
688	    shape checks (mirroring the evolution summary endpoint).
689	    """
690	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
691	
692	    version_rows = conn.execute(
693	        "SELECT id, version FROM schema_versions WHERE dataset_id = ?",
694	        (dataset["id"],),
695	    ).fetchall()
696	    ordered = sorted(version_rows, key=lambda row: row["version"])
697	    definitions = [
698	        _version_field_definitions(conn, row["id"]) for row in ordered
699	    ]
700	    if not any(field_name in fields for fields in definitions):
701	        raise NotFoundError(
702	            f"Field '{field_name}' does not exist in any schema version of "
703	            f"dataset '{dataset_name}'"
704	        )
705	
706	    if body:
707	        raise RequestInvalidError(
708	            "The field trajectory endpoint does not accept a request body"
709	        )
710	    if query_keys:
711	        raise RequestInvalidError(
712	            "The field trajectory endpoint does not accept query parameters"
713	        )
714	
715	    entries = [
716	        {"version": row["version"], "definition": fields.get(field_name)}
717	        for row, fields in zip(ordered, definitions)
718	    ]
719	
720	    changes: list[dict] = []
721	    for index, (base_row, target_row) in enumerate(zip(ordered, ordered[1:])):
722	        before = definitions[index].get(field_name)
723	        after = definitions[index + 1].get(field_name)
724	        # The base version's same-named field starts the traversal when it
725	        # exists; the target version's joins when it exists (the same
726	        # start-field rule as the compatibility impact response).
727	        start_ids = []
728	        if before is not None:
729	            start_ids.append(_field_id_by_name(conn, base_row["id"], field_name))
730	        if after is not None:
731	            start_ids.append(
732	                _field_id_by_name(conn, target_row["id"], field_name)
733	            )
734	        impacted = _compute_impacted_multi(
735	            conn, [field_id for field_id in start_ids if field_id is not None]
736	        )
737	        changes.append(
738	            {
739	                "base_version": base_row["version"],
740	                "target_version": target_row["version"],
741	                "status": _field_status_change(before, after),
742	                "impacted": impacted,
743	                "impacted_datasets": sorted(
744	                    {item["dataset"] for item in impacted}
745	                ),
746	            }
747	        )
748	
749	    return {
750	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
751	        "field": field_name,
752	        "entries": entries,
753	        "changes": changes,
754	    }

792	def create_lineage_link(
793	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
794	    *,
795	    target_dataset: str,
796	    target_version: int,
797	    target_field: str,
798	    source_dataset: str,
799	    source_version: int,
800	    source_field: str,
801	) -> dict:
802	    target = require_dataset(conn, target_dataset, role="Target dataset")
803	    source = require_dataset(conn, source_dataset, role="Source dataset")
804	
805	    if source["id"] == target["id"]:
806	        raise RequestInvalidError("Source and target datasets must be different")
807	
808	    target_version_id, target_field_id = _require_field(
809	        conn, target, target_version, target_field, role="Target"
810	    )
811	    source_version_id, source_field_id = _require_field(
812	        conn, source, source_version, source_field, role="Source"
813	    )
814	
815	    existing = conn.execute(
816	        "SELECT id FROM lineage_links WHERE target_field_id = ? AND source_field_id = ?",
817	        (target_field_id, source_field_id),
818	    ).fetchone()
819	    if existing is not None:
820	        raise ConflictError(
821	            "This field mapping has already been registered: "
822	            f"'{source_dataset}' v{source_version}.{source_field} -> "
823	            f"'{target_dataset}' v{target_version}.{target_field}"
824	        )
825	
826	    try:
827	        conn.execute(
828	            "INSERT INTO lineage_links ("
829	            "target_dataset_id, target_version_id, target_field_id, "
830	            "source_dataset_id, source_version_id, source_field_id, created_at"
831	            ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
832	            (
833	                target["id"],
834	                target_version_id,
835	                target_field_id,
836	                source["id"],
837	                source_version_id,
838	                source_field_id,
839	                utc_now_iso(),
840	            ),
841	        )
842	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
843	        raise ConflictError("This field mapping has already been registered") from exc
844	
845	    # The new edge can only extend the impact of fields that reach its source.
846	    _invalidate_impact_cache_for_upstream(
847	        conn, source["name"], source_version, source_field, source_field_id
848	    )
849	
850	    return {
851	        "target_dataset": target["name"],
852	        "target_version": target_version,
853	        "target_field": target_field,
854	        "source": {
855	            "dataset": source["name"],
856	            "version": source_version,
857	            "field": source_field,
858	        },
859	    }

861	
862	# The six locating fields of a lineage mapping, in body key order; the
863	# deletion request carries exactly these.
864	_LINEAGE_MAPPING_FIELDS = (
865	    "target_dataset",
866	    "target_version",
867	    "target_field",
868	    "source_dataset",
869	    "source_version",
870	    "source_field",
871	)

873	
874	def delete_lineage_link(
875	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
876	    dataset_name: str,
877	    version: int,
878	    *,
879	    body: bytes = b"",
880	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
881	) -> dict:
882	    """Delete one registered lineage mapping, returning the removed mapping.
883	
884	    The request body has the same shape as registration: the six locating
885	    fields name the complete mapping to delete and the target must agree with
886	    the path. Validation runs in two phases. First every locating value
887	    readable in the request (path plus whatever the body carries) is resolved,
888	    so an unknown dataset, version or field is a 404 ahead of every
889	    request-shape error — including when all six values name existing
890	    resources but the mapping itself was never registered. Only then is the
891	    request shape judged: an empty or whitespace body, invalid JSON, a
892	    non-object payload, missing or extra fields, wrong types, blank names and
893	    any query parameter are all 422, as are a mapping whose source and target
894	    datasets coincide or whose body target disagrees with the path. No
895	    rejection writes anything: the lineage graph, the impact cache and every
896	    other metadata table are left untouched (the transaction rolls back).
897	
898	    A registered mapping is deleted atomically: concurrent deletes of the
899	    same mapping succeed exactly once, the loser gets a 404 and changes
900	    nothing. The impact cache invalidation matches registration — the cached
901	    impacts of the mapping's source field and of every field that can reach
902	    it are dropped and rebuilt on the next read; unrelated entries are kept.
903	    """
904	    # Take the write lock before any read so two concurrent deletes of the
905	    # same mapping cannot race a read-then-upgrade: the loser blocks here
906	    # until the winner commits, then observes the committed delete and
907	    # reports 404 without changing anything.
908	    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
909	
910	    # The path dataset and version resolve first, so an unknown path target
911	    # is a 404 ahead of every request-shape error.
912	    path_dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name, role="Target dataset")
913	    _require_schema_version(conn, path_dataset, version)
914	
915	    # Best-effort read of the body's locating values: whatever can be read
916	    # drives resource lookups before any shape validation. An unreadable
917	    # (missing, blank or wrongly typed) value simply skips its lookup and is
918	    # reported as a 422 in the second phase.
919	    payload: Any = None
920	    if body.strip():
921	        try:
922	            payload = json.loads(body)
923	        except ValueError:
924	            payload = None
925	    values = payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}
926	
927	    def readable_name(key: str) -> str | None:
928	        value = values.get(key)
929	        return value if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip() else None
930	
931	    def readable_version(key: str) -> int | None:
932	        value = values.get(key)
933	        return (
934	            value if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) else None
935	        )
936	
937	    # Target side: the dataset defaults to the path dataset (the body target
938	    # must agree with it anyway) so a readable body version is still looked
939	    # up when the body does not name the dataset.
940	    target_dataset = path_dataset
941	    body_target_dataset = readable_name("target_dataset")
942	    if body_target_dataset is not None:
943	        target_dataset = require_dataset(
944	            conn, body_target_dataset, role="Target dataset"
945	        )
946	    body_target_version = readable_version("target_version")
947	    if body_target_version is not None:
948	        target_version_row = conn.execute(
949	            "SELECT id FROM schema_versions WHERE dataset_id = ? AND version = ?",
950	            (target_dataset["id"], body_target_version),
951	        ).fetchone()
952	        if target_version_row is None:
953	            raise NotFoundError(
954	                f"Target schema version {body_target_version} of dataset "
955	                f"'{target_dataset['name']}' does not exist"
956	            )
957	        body_target_field = readable_name("target_field")
958	        if body_target_field is not None:
959	            target_field_row = conn.execute(
960	                "SELECT id FROM schema_fields WHERE version_id = ? AND name = ?",
961	                (target_version_row["id"], body_target_field),
962	            ).fetchone()
963	            if target_field_row is None:
964	                raise NotFoundError(
965	                    f"Target field '{body_target_field}' does not exist in "
966	                    f"version {body_target_version} of dataset "
967	                    f"'{target_dataset['name']}'"
968	                )
969	
970	    # Source side: each lookup needs the parent resource, so the chain only
971	    # advances while the locating values stay readable.
972	    body_source_dataset = readable_name("source_dataset")
973	    if body_source_dataset is not None:
974	        source_dataset = require_dataset(
975	            conn, body_source_dataset, role="Source dataset"
976	        )
977	        body_source_version = readable_version("source_version")
978	        if body_source_version is not None:
979	            source_version_row = conn.execute(
980	                "SELECT id FROM schema_versions "
981	                "WHERE dataset_id = ? AND version = ?",
982	                (source_dataset["id"], body_source_version),
983	            ).fetchone()
984	            if source_version_row is None:
985	                raise NotFoundError(
986	                    f"Source schema version {body_source_version} of dataset "
987	                    f"'{source_dataset['name']}' does not exist"
988	                )
989	            body_source_field = readable_name("source_field")
990	            if body_source_field is not None:
991	                source_field_row = conn.execute(
992	                    "SELECT id FROM schema_fields "
993	                    "WHERE version_id = ? AND name = ?",
994	                    (source_version_row["id"], body_source_field),
995	                ).fetchone()
996	                if source_field_row is None:
997	                    raise NotFoundError(
998	                        f"Source field '{body_source_field}' does not exist in "
999	                        f"version {body_source_version} of dataset "
1000	                        f"'{source_dataset['name']}'"
1001	                    )
1002	
1003	    # Every resource named by a readable locating value exists; only now is
1004	    # the request shape judged.
1005	    if query_keys:
1006	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1007	            "The lineage deletion endpoint does not accept query parameters"
1008	        )
1009	    if not body.strip():
1010	        raise RequestInvalidError("Request body must not be empty")
1011	    if payload is None:
1012	        raise RequestInvalidError("Request body is not valid JSON")
1013	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
1014	        raise RequestInvalidError("Request body must be a JSON object")
1015	    missing = [key for key in _LINEAGE_MAPPING_FIELDS if key not in payload]
1016	    if missing:
1017	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1018	            "Request body is incomplete: missing field(s) " + ", ".join(missing)
1019	        )
1020	    unknown = sorted(key for key in payload if key not in _LINEAGE_MAPPING_FIELDS)
1021	    if unknown:
1022	        raise RequestInvalidError("Unknown field(s): " + ", ".join(unknown))
1023	    for key in ("target_dataset", "target_field", "source_dataset", "source_field"):
1024	        value = payload[key]
1025	        if not isinstance(value, str):
1026	            raise RequestInvalidError(f"Field '{key}' must be a string")
1027	        if not value.strip():
1028	            raise RequestInvalidError(f"Field '{key}' must be a non-empty name")

1030	        value = payload[key]

1033	
1034	    if payload["source_dataset"] == payload["target_dataset"]:

1036	    if payload["target_dataset"] != dataset_name or payload["target_version"] != version:
1037	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1038	            "Target dataset and version in the body must match the request path"
1039	        )
1040	
1041	    # The shape is fully valid, so every locating value was resolved in the
1042	    # first phase and these lookups cannot fail.
1043	    target_dataset = require_dataset(conn, payload["target_dataset"], role="Target dataset")
1044	    source_dataset = require_dataset(conn, payload["source_dataset"], role="Source dataset")
1045	    _, target_field_id = _require_field(
1046	        conn, target_dataset, payload["target_version"], payload["target_field"],
1047	        role="Target",
1048	    )
1049	    _, source_field_id = _require_field(
1050	        conn, source_dataset, payload["source_version"], payload["source_field"],
1051	        role="Source",
1052	    )

1054	    # Dropping the edge shrinks the impact of exactly the fields that can

1056	    # source field and everything upstream of it. The reverse walk runs
1057	    # before the delete, while the edge still exists.

1059	        conn,

1061	        payload["source_version"],
1062	        payload["source_field"],
1063	        source_field_id,
1064	    )
1065	
1066	    deleted = conn.execute(
1067	        "DELETE FROM lineage_links "
1068	        "WHERE target_field_id = ? AND source_field_id = ?",
1069	        (target_field_id, source_field_id),
1070	    )

1080	            f"v{payload['target_version']}.{payload['target_field']}"
1081	        )

1084	        "target_dataset": target_dataset["name"],
1085	        "target_version": payload["target_version"],
1086	        "target_field": payload["target_field"],
1087	        "source": {
1088	            "dataset": source_dataset["name"],
1089	            "version": payload["source_version"],
1090	            "field": payload["source_field"],
1091	        },

1155	def _lineage_forward_edges(
1156	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1157	) -> dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]]:
1158	    """Adjacency of the lineage graph: source field id -> target field refs."""
1159	    rows = conn.execute(
1160	        """
1161	        SELECT  ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
1162	                ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
1163	                td.name            AS target_dataset,
1164	                tv.version         AS target_version,
1165	                tf.name            AS target_field
1166	        FROM    lineage_links ll
1167	        JOIN    datasets td ON td.id = ll.target_dataset_id
1168	        JOIN    schema_versions tv ON tv.id = ll.target_version_id
1169	        JOIN    schema_fields tf ON tf.id = ll.target_field_id
1170	        """
1171	    ).fetchall()
1172	    edges: dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]] = {}
1173	    for row in rows:
1174	        ref = {
1175	            "dataset": row["target_dataset"],
1176	            "version": row["target_version"],
1177	            "field": row["target_field"],
1178	        }
1179	        edges.setdefault(row["source_field_id"], []).append(
1180	            (row["target_field_id"], ref)
1181	        )
1182	    return edges

1185	def _impacted_from_edges(
1186	    edges: dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]], source_field_id: int
1187	) -> list[dict]:
1188	    """All fields reachable downstream of the source, deduplicated and sorted.
1189	
1190	    The source field id is seeded into the visited set, so cycles terminate
1191	    and the source itself never appears in the result.
1192	    """
1193	    visited = {source_field_id}
1194	    impacted: dict[tuple[str, int, str], dict] = {}
1195	    queue = [source_field_id]
1196	    while queue:
1197	        current = queue.pop()
1198	        for target_field_id, ref in edges.get(current, ()):
1199	            if target_field_id in visited:
1200	                continue
1201	            visited.add(target_field_id)
1202	            impacted[(ref["dataset"], ref["version"], ref["field"])] = ref
1203	            queue.append(target_field_id)
1204	    return [impacted[key] for key in sorted(impacted)]
1205

1207	def _compute_impacted(conn: sqlite3.Connection, source_field_id: int) -> list[dict]:
1208	    """All fields reachable downstream of the source over the current graph."""
1209	    return _impacted_from_edges(_lineage_forward_edges(conn), source_field_id)

1262	def _invalidate_impact_cache_for_upstream(
1263	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1264	    source_dataset: str,
1265	    source_version: int,
1266	    source_field: str,
1267	    source_field_id: int,
1268	) -> None:
1269	    """Invalidate cached impacts of the new link's source and its upstream.
1270	
1271	    A new mapping ``source -> target`` only changes the impact result of
1272	    fields that can reach ``source`` (``source`` itself included), so exactly
1273	    those cached entries are dropped; unrelated entries are kept. The reverse
1274	    walk runs after the link was inserted so cycles are covered too.
1275	    """
1276	    rows = conn.execute(
1277	        """
1278	        SELECT  ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
1279	                ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
1280	                sd.name            AS source_dataset,
1281	                sv.version         AS source_version,
1282	                sf.name            AS source_field
1283	        FROM    lineage_links ll
1284	        JOIN    datasets sd ON sd.id = ll.source_dataset_id
1285	        JOIN    schema_versions sv ON sv.id = ll.source_version_id
1286	        JOIN    schema_fields sf ON sf.id = ll.source_field_id
1287	        """
1288	    ).fetchall()
1289	    reverse: dict[int, list[sqlite3.Row]] = {}
1290	    for row in rows:
1291	        reverse.setdefault(row["target_field_id"], []).append(row)
1292	
1293	    visited = {source_field_id}
1294	    upstream = {(source_dataset, source_version, source_field)}
1295	    queue = [source_field_id]
1296	    while queue:
1297	        current = queue.pop()
1298	        for row in reverse.get(current, ()):
1299	            if row["source_field_id"] in visited:
1300	                continue
1301	            visited.add(row["source_field_id"])
1302	            upstream.add(
1303	                (row["source_dataset"], row["source_version"], row["source_field"])
1304	            )
1305	            queue.append(row["source_field_id"])
1306	
1307	    conn.executemany(
1308	        "DELETE FROM lineage_impact_cache "
1309	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
1310	        sorted(upstream),
1311	    )

1314	def get_lineage_impact(
1315	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1316	    dataset_name: str,
1317	    version: int,
1318	    field: str,
1319	    *,
1320	    field_values: tuple[str, ...] = (),

1323	    version_row = conn.execute(
1324	        "SELECT id FROM schema_versions WHERE dataset_id = ? AND version = ?",
1325	        (dataset["id"], version),
1326	    ).fetchone()
1327	    if version_row is None:
1328	        raise NotFoundError(
1329	            f"Source schema version {version} of dataset "
1330	            f"'{dataset['name']}' does not exist"
1331	        )
1332	
1333	    # A repeated 'field' parameter is a 422 and is judged before the field
1334	    # lookup, so the second value's field resolution can never preempt it
1335	    # with a 404.
1336	    if len(field_values) > 1:
1337	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1338	            "Query parameter 'field' must be provided exactly once"
1339	        )
1340	
1341	    field_row = conn.execute(
1342	        "SELECT id FROM schema_fields WHERE version_id = ? AND name = ?",
1343	        (version_row["id"], field),
1344	    ).fetchone()

1348	            f"{version} of dataset '{dataset['name']}'"

1351

1355	        _impact_cache_store(conn, dataset["name"], version, field, impacted)
1356

1358	        "source": {"dataset": dataset["name"], "version": version, "field": field},
1359	        "impacted": impacted,
1360	    }

1364	# Lineage impact cache consistency audit (read-only)
1365	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
1366	
1367	
1368	def audit_lineage_impact_cache(
1369	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1370	    dataset_name: str,
1371	    version_number: int,
1372	    *,
1373	    body: bytes = b"",
1374	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
1375	) -> dict:
1376	    """Read-only per-field consistency audit of one version's impact cache.
1377	
1378	    Every field of the version is audited in name order. A field without a
1379	    cache record is ``missing`` — a normal state for a field whose impact was
1380	    never queried, not an error. A cached field is recomputed with the exact
1381	    impact-query traversal (``_compute_impacted``: downstream fields merged
1382	    and deduplicated, the start field excluded, cycles terminating) and is
1383	    ``cached`` only when the stored record equals the recomputed result;
1384	    otherwise it is ``mismatch``.
1385	
1386	    The audit computes on every read and never writes: no cache record is
1387	    inserted, invalidated or repaired, so impact queries, path explanations
1388	    and source-path reads behave exactly as before under the same lineage
1389	    data. The path dataset/version resolves first (404); only afterwards are
1390	    any request body bytes — whitespace-only included — or any query
1391	    parameter rejected with 422, preserving the impact query's 404-before-422
1392	    precedence.
1393	    """
1394	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1395	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1396	
1397	    if body:
1398	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1399	            "The lineage impact cache audit endpoint does not accept a "
1400	            "request body"
1401	        )
1402	    if query_keys:
1403	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1404	            "The lineage impact cache audit endpoint does not accept query "
1405	            "parameters"
1406	        )
1407	
1408	    field_rows = conn.execute(
1409	        "SELECT id, name FROM schema_fields WHERE version_id = ? ORDER BY name",
1410	        (version_row["id"],),
1411	    ).fetchall()
1412	    cache_rows = conn.execute(
1413	        "SELECT source_field, impacted FROM lineage_impact_cache "
1414	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ?",
1415	        (dataset["name"], version_number),
1416	    ).fetchall()
1417	    cached_by_field = {
1418	        row["source_field"]: json.loads(row["impacted"]) for row in cache_rows
1419	    }
1420	
1421	    # Build the forward graph once; each cached field's expected result then
1422	    # walks it with the exact impact-query traversal (the start id is seeded
1423	    # visited, so cycles terminate and the start field never appears).
1424	    edges = _lineage_forward_edges(conn)
1425	
1426	    entries: list[dict] = []
1427	    counts = {"cached_count": 0, "missing_count": 0, "mismatch_count": 0}
1428	    for field_row in field_rows:
1429	        field_name = field_row["name"]
1430	        if field_name not in cached_by_field:
1431	            status = "missing"
1432	        else:
1433	            recomputed = _impacted_from_edges(edges, field_row["id"])
1434	            status = (
1435	                "cached"
1436	                if cached_by_field[field_name] == recomputed
1437	                else "mismatch"
1438	            )
1439	        entries.append({"field": field_name, "status": status})
1440	        counts[f"{status}_count"] += 1
1441	
1442	    return {
1443	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
1444	        "version": version_number,
1445	        "entries": entries,
1446	        "counts": counts,
1447	    }

1500	            "field": row["source_field"],

1508	def _shortest_lineage_paths(
1509	    edges: dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]],
1510	    refs: dict[int, dict],
1511	    start_field_id: int,
1512	) -> list[dict]:
1513	    """Shortest path from the start field to every field reachable along edges.
1514	
1515	    Breadth-first traversal over the lineage graph guarantees the minimum
1516	    number of edges; each node's outgoing links are expanded in location-key
1517	    (dataset, version, field) order, so the first discovery of a node is the
1518	    lexicographically smallest node sequence among its shortest paths. The
1519	    start id is seeded as visited, so cycles terminate and the start itself
1520	    never appears in the result. Every ordering is computed explicitly here
1521	    rather than read from database order.
1522	    """
1523	    for targets in edges.values():
1524	        targets.sort(
1525	            key=lambda item: (
1526	                item[1]["dataset"],
1527	                item[1]["version"],
1528	                item[1]["field"],
1529	            )
1530	        )
1531	
1532	    shortest: dict[int, list[dict]] = {start_field_id: [refs[start_field_id]]}
1533	    queue = deque([start_field_id])
1534	    while queue:
1535	        current = queue.popleft()
1536	        current_path = shortest[current]
1537	        for next_field_id, ref in edges.get(current, ()):
1538	            if next_field_id in shortest:
1539	                continue
1540	            shortest[next_field_id] = current_path + [ref]
1541	            queue.append(next_field_id)
1542	
1543	    items: list[dict] = []
1544	    for field_id in sorted(
1545	        (fid for fid in shortest if fid != start_field_id),
1546	        key=lambda fid: (
1547	            refs[fid]["dataset"],
1548	            refs[fid]["version"],
1549	            refs[fid]["field"],
1550	        ),
1551	    ):
1552	        path = shortest[field_id]
1553	        items.append(
1554	            {
1555	                "dataset": path[-1]["dataset"],
1556	                "version": path[-1]["version"],
1557	                "field": path[-1]["field"],
1558	                "path": path,
1559	                "path_length": len(path) - 1,
1560	            }
1561	        )
1562	    return items
1563	
1564	
1565	def _compute_impact_paths(
1566	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, source_field_id: int
1567	) -> list[dict]:
1568	    """Shortest lineage path from the source to every downstream field."""
1569	    return _shortest_lineage_paths(
1570	        _lineage_forward_edges(conn), _lineage_field_refs(conn), source_field_id
1571	    )

1576	) -> list[dict]:

1578	    return _shortest_lineage_paths(
1579	        _lineage_reverse_edges(conn), _lineage_field_refs(conn), target_field_id
1580	    )
